default.$description: Main page/app surface. Not for cards, popovers, or elevated layers.

docs.description: Main surface of the page — the background of `<html>` and root containers.
docs.do: Use as the background of the root page and the main containers (`<body>`, `<main>`).
docs.dont: Do not use for cards, popovers or raised surfaces — use `color.background.subtle` or `color.background.elevated`.

subtle.$description: Recessed or secondary surface (cards, muted areas, secondary). Not for the main page surface.

docs.description: A slightly muted secondary surface that creates visual hierarchy.
docs.do: Use for cards, muted areas, secondary sidebars, inner panels.
docs.dont: Do not use for the page's main background.

elevated.$description: Raised surface above the default layer (popovers, dropdowns, dialogs). Not for inline card surfaces.

docs.description: A floating surface above the main content.
docs.do: Use for popovers, drop-downs, dialogs, light tooltips.
docs.dont: Do not use for inline cards — they are not "raised" on the Z axis.

inverse.$description: Inverted surface for contrast callouts. Not for general-purpose backgrounds.

docs.description: An inverted surface that contrasts strongly with the main background.
docs.do: Use for dark tooltips, inverted badges, alert banners.
docs.dont: Do not use as a general page background — it is reserved for occasional inverted surfaces.

default.$description: Primary body and heading text. Not for secondary, placeholder, or disabled text.

docs.description: Main text color for body text and headings.
docs.do: Use for all main content text, titles and important labels.
docs.dont: Do not lower the opacity to fake secondary text — use `color.text.subtle`.

subtle.$description: Secondary or supporting text (captions, helper text, metadata). Not for primary readable content.

docs.description: Secondary text, captions, helper text, metadata.
docs.do: Use for field labels, form descriptions, timestamps.
docs.dont: Do not use for main body content — its contrast is too low for long reading.

bold.$description: Emphatic text with stronger contrast when needed. Not for subtle or secondary text.

docs.description: High-contrast emphasized text — for emphasis where `text.default` is not enough.
docs.do: Use for emphasis in areas with a busy visual context.
docs.dont: Do not use as a substitute for `text.default` in standard body text.

inverse.$description: Text on top of inverse (dark) surfaces. Not for default surface text.

docs.description: Text on an inverse surface (a dark background in light mode, a light one in dark mode).
docs.do: Use only on `color.background.inverse`.
docs.dont: Do not use on standard surfaces — the contrast would be too low.

default.$description: Text conveying a primary action (links, active button labels). Not for generic body text.

docs.description: Primary action text — links, active navigation labels.
docs.do: Use for text links and labels that express a clickable action.
docs.dont: Do not use for generic body text — it is reserved for actionable elements.

on.$description: Text rendered on top of a primary action background. Not for text on neutral surfaces.

docs.description: Text on a `color.action.background.default` background.
docs.do: Use for the label of a primary button.
docs.dont: Do not use on neutral surfaces — the contrast is too low on a light background.

default.$description: Error, danger, or destructive action text and icons, on a neutral surface or on a destructive tint. Not for general warning or informational text.

docs.description: Destructive or error-state text and icons — the class `text-destructive`. Darker than `color.feedback.error.default` in light mode and lighter in dark mode, so it stays at 4.5:1 or more on every surface and on the `bg-destructive/10`–`/30` tints.
docs.do: Use for error validation messages, destructive button and badge labels, and destructive menu items.
docs.dont: Do not use for warnings or information — it is reserved for critical errors. Do not use `color.feedback.error.default` for text: on a card or a destructive tint it falls below 4.5:1.

default.$description: Success text and icons, on a neutral surface or on a success tint. Not for warnings, errors or neutral information.

docs.description: Success-state text and icons — the class `text-success`. Darker than `color.feedback.success.default` in light mode and lighter in dark mode, so it stays at 4.5:1 or more on every surface and on the `bg-success/10`–`/30` tints.
docs.do: Use for the success Alert and Badge, and for a confirmation message next to its field.
docs.dont: Do not carry the meaning by color alone: a success and an error are hard to tell apart for a red-green color-blind reader, so an icon or a word says it too. Do not use `color.feedback.success.default` for text.

default.$description: Warning text and icons, on a neutral surface or on a warning tint. Not for errors, successes or neutral information.

docs.description: Warning-state text and icons — the class `text-warning`. It stays at 4.5:1 or more on every surface and on the `bg-warning/10`–`/30` tints, where the warning fill itself does not reach 3:1 on a light surface.
docs.do: Use for the warning Alert and Badge, and for the icon of any warning: the fill is too light to stand alone.
docs.dont: Do not use for errors — a blocking problem is destructive. Do not use `color.feedback.warning.default` for text, borders or icons.

default.$description: Standard dividers and component outlines. Not for input fields or focus rings.

docs.description: Standard border for separators and component outlines.
docs.do: Use for dividers between sections and card outlines.
docs.dont: Do not use for form fields — use `color.border.input`.

subtle.$description: Lightweight dividers where minimal visual weight is preferred. Not for interactive element borders.

docs.description: A discreet, low-weight border.
docs.do: Use for inner list separators and light divisions.
docs.dont: Do not use on interactive components that need a visible border.

input.$description: Border for form input fields. Not for decorative dividers or layout borders.

docs.description: The border of form fields.
docs.do: Use for every `<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>` and `<checkbox>` border.
docs.dont: Do not use for decorative separators — it is reserved for form controls.

focus.$description: Focus ring outline for keyboard accessibility. Not for resting or hover states.

docs.description: Focus ring for keyboard accessibility (`:focus-visible`).
docs.do: Use only for the `:focus-visible` state of interactive elements.
docs.dont: Never remove the focus ring — it is a WCAG 2.4.7 accessibility requirement.

default.$description: Standard icon fill. Not for icons in branded or destructive contexts.

docs.description: Standard icon color in a neutral context.
docs.do: Use for navigation, standard action and content icons.
docs.dont: Do not use for icons inside primary buttons — use `color.icon.action`.

subtle.$description: Muted/secondary icon fill. Not for primary interactive icons.

docs.description: A secondary, decorative or muted icon.
docs.do: Use for status icons, loading indicators and metadata icons.
docs.dont: Do not use for main action icons.

action.$description: Icon on a primary action background. Not for icons on neutral surfaces.

docs.description: An icon on a primary action background.
docs.do: Use for icons inside primary buttons or action badges.
docs.dont: Do not use on a neutral or light background.

default.$description: Primary call-to-action button/element background. Not for secondary or ghost variants.

docs.description: Background of the primary CTA component.
docs.do: Use for the background of primary buttons and CTA elements.
docs.dont: Do not use for the secondary, ghost or outline variants — those variants have no colored background.

foreground.$description: Text or icon on top of a primary action background. Not for text on neutral surfaces.

docs.description: Text or icon on a primary action background.
docs.do: Always pair with `color.action.background.default` for the text of a primary button.
docs.dont: Do not use on a neutral or light background.

default.$description: Error state color for backgrounds, tints and borders. Not for text, warnings or success states.

docs.description: Error-state fill — solid or tinted background, border, focus ring.
docs.do: Use for the borders and rings of invalid fields and for the `bg-destructive/10`–`/30` tints.
docs.dont: Do not use for text or icons — use `color.text.destructive.default` (`text-destructive`). Do not use for warnings or success states.

foreground.$description: Text and icons placed on color.feedback.error.default. Never use color.text.default on an error surface.

docs.description: Text and icons placed **on** a solid error surface.
docs.do: Use whenever a solid `bg-destructive` background carries text or an icon.
docs.dont: Never put `color.text.default` or `text-white` on an error surface — in dark mode, white on red.500 drops to 2.89:1.

default.$description: Success state color for backgrounds, tints and borders. Not for text, warnings or errors.

docs.description: Success-state fill — solid or tinted background, border.
docs.do: Use for the `bg-success/10`–`/30` tints and for a solid `bg-success` surface with `text-success-foreground`.
docs.dont: Do not use for text or icons — use `color.text.success.default` (`text-success`). Do not use for warnings or errors.

foreground.$description: Text and icons placed on color.feedback.success.default. Never use color.text.default on a success surface.

docs.description: Text and icons placed **on** a solid success surface.
docs.do: Use whenever a solid `bg-success` background carries text or an icon.
docs.dont: Never put `text-white` on a success surface — in dark mode the fill is light and needs dark text.

default.$description: Warning state color for backgrounds and tints. Not for text, borders or icons, not for errors or successes.

docs.description: Warning-state fill — solid or tinted background. At 1.92:1 on white in light mode, it never stands alone as a border or an icon.
docs.do: Use for the `bg-warning/10`–`/30` tints and for a solid `bg-warning` surface with `text-warning-foreground`.
docs.dont: Do not use for text, icons or a lone border — use `color.text.warning.default` (`text-warning`). Do not use for errors.

foreground.$description: Text and icons placed on color.feedback.warning.default, dark in both modes. Never use white on a warning surface.

docs.description: Text and icons placed **on** a solid warning surface — dark in both modes.
docs.do: Use whenever a solid `bg-warning` background carries text or an icon.
docs.dont: Never put `text-white` on a warning surface: white on the light-mode fill is below 2:1.

1.$description: Categorical chart Series 1 — the brand violet. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

2.$description: Categorical chart Series 2 — blue. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

3.$description: Categorical chart Series 3 — ochre, yellow in dark mode. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

4.$description: Categorical chart Series 4 — plum. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

5.$description: Categorical chart Series 5 — brown, gold in dark mode. For unordered categories: every series is at least 3:1 on the default and subtle surfaces of its mode, and distinguishable from the others under protanopia and deuteranopia (lint-chart-palette). Not for ordered data — use color.chart.sequential.*.

docs.description: Categorical palette for chart series (unordered categories); ordered data uses `color.chart.sequential.*`.
docs.do: Use in order (1 → 5) for chart series.
docs.dont: Do not reuse these tokens for general UI colors — they are reserved for data visualization.

1.$description: Sequential chart step 1 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.

2.$description: Sequential chart step 2 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.

3.$description: Sequential chart step 3 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.

4.$description: Sequential chart step 4 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.

5.$description: Sequential chart step 5 of 5, lightest to darkest. Ordered data only (a heatmap, a scale of intensity): its steps differ by lightness, not hue, so they cannot tell unordered categories apart.

background.$description: Sidebar panel surface. Not for the main content area or popovers.

foreground.$description: Default text and icon color within the sidebar. Not for sidebar accent or muted items.

border.$description: Sidebar internal divider/border. Not for content-area borders.

ring.$description: Focus ring within the sidebar. Not for main content focus rings.

default.$description: Active/primary nav item background in the sidebar. Not for generic sidebar items.

on.$description: Text on top of the sidebar primary active item. Not for inactive item text.

default.$description: Hovered or secondary sidebar item background. Not for the active primary item.

foreground.$description: Text on sidebar accent (hover) surfaces. Not for primary active item text.

docs.do: Use only in side navigation components.
docs.dont: Do not reuse these tokens in the main content — they belong to the sidebar's context.

white.$description: White that stays white in both modes: a slider thumb, text on a photo. Not for surfaces — use color.background.* so dark mode applies.

black.$description: Black that stays black in both modes, used with an opacity modifier for scrims behind modals (bg-black/10). Not for text or surfaces.

xs.$description: Extra-small component padding/gap (4px). Not for layout or section spacing.

docs.do: Reserved: nothing reads it, and it has no class. Inside a component, use the spacing scale (`gap-1`, 4px).
docs.dont: Do not use for layout spacing.

sm.$description: Small component padding/gap (8px). Not for layout or section spacing.

docs.do: Reserved: nothing reads it, and it has no class. Inside a component, use the spacing scale (`gap-2`, 8px).
docs.dont: Do not use to space out page sections.

md.$description: Medium component padding/gap (16px). Not for layout or section spacing.

docs.do: Reserved: nothing reads it, and it has no class. Inside a component, use the spacing scale (`p-4`, 16px).
docs.dont: Do not use for the gap between page sections.

lg.$description: Large component spacing (24px), read through var(): the viewport gutter of DialogContent. Not for layout or section spacing.

docs.do: The room DialogContent keeps from the viewport edges (`max-w-[calc(100%-var(--space-component-lg))]`); it has no class.
docs.dont: Do not confuse with `space.layout.page-padding` (same value, different context).

xl.$description: Extra-large component padding/gap (32px). Not for layout or section spacing.

docs.do: Reserved: nothing reads it, and it has no class. Inside a component, use the spacing scale (`p-8`, 32px).
docs.dont: Do not use between nearby inline elements.

0-5.$description: Spacing step 0.5 (2px): the `0.5` step of the Tailwind spacing scale, for padding, margin, gap, inset, translate and sizes.

1.$description: Spacing step 1 (4px): the `1` step of the Tailwind spacing scale, for padding, margin, gap, inset, translate and sizes.

20.$description: Spacing step 20 (80px): the `20` step of the Tailwind spacing scale, for padding, margin, gap, inset, translate and sizes.

24.$description: Spacing step 24 (96px): the `24` step of the Tailwind spacing scale, for padding, margin, gap, inset, translate and sizes.

3xs.$description: Container width 3xs (256px): the value Tailwind compiles into `max-w-3xs` and `@3xs:`, which lint-theme-bridge checks equals the token. Nothing in the design system draws with it yet.

2xs.$description: Container width 2xs (288px): the value Tailwind compiles into `max-w-2xs` and `@2xs:`, which lint-theme-bridge checks equals the token. Nothing in the design system draws with it yet.

xs.$description: Container width xs (320px), for a max-width or a width that holds content. Tailwind compiles this value into `max-w-xs` and `@xs:` itself; lint-theme-bridge checks it equals the token.

sm.$description: Container width sm (384px), for a max-width or a width that holds content. Tailwind compiles this value into `max-w-sm` and `@sm:` itself; lint-theme-bridge checks it equals the token.

md.$description: Container width md (448px), for a max-width or a width that holds content. Tailwind compiles this value into `max-w-md` and `@md:` itself; lint-theme-bridge checks it equals the token.

lg.$description: Container width lg (512px): the value Tailwind compiles into `max-w-lg` and `@lg:`, which lint-theme-bridge checks equals the token. Nothing in the design system draws with it yet.

xl.$description: Container width xl (576px): the value Tailwind compiles into `max-w-xl` and `@xl:`, which lint-theme-bridge checks equals the token. Nothing in the design system draws with it yet.

7xl.$description: Container width 7xl (1280px): the value Tailwind compiles into `max-w-7xl` and `@7xl:`, which lint-theme-bridge checks equals the token. Nothing in the design system draws with it yet.

focus-ring-width.$description: Width of the focus ring indicator (2px). Use for all focus-visible ring styles.

page-padding.$description: Horizontal padding for the main page container. Not for component-level spacing.

docs.do: Horizontal padding of the root page container.
docs.dont: Do not apply to inner components.

section-gap.$description: Vertical gap between major page sections. Not for component-level spacing.

docs.do: Vertical space between the major sections of a page.
docs.dont: Do not use between components of the same section.

content-sm.$description: Narrow content column max-width (42rem). Not for full-width or wide layouts.

docs.do: `max-w-[var(--space-layout-content-sm)]` for editorial pages.
docs.dont: Do not use as a padding value.

content-default.$description: Default content column max-width (64rem). Not for narrow or wide layouts.

docs.do: The main content container of most pages.
docs.dont: Do not exceed it for standard content layouts.

content-lg.$description: Wide content column max-width (80rem). Not for narrow or default layouts.

docs.do: Dashboards, data tables, multi-column layouts.
docs.dont: Do not use for editorial content pages.

sidebar.$description: Default sidebar width (16rem). Use for the main navigation sidebar.

sidebar-mobile.$description: Sidebar width on mobile viewports (18rem). Slightly wider for touch targets.

xs.$description: Extra-small text size (12px). Use for labels, badges, captions.

sm.$description: Small text size (14px). Use for secondary content and UI labels.

base.$description: Default body text size (16px). Use for main readable content.

lg.$description: Large text size (18px). Use for featured body text.

xl.$description: XL text (20px). Use for section headings.

3xl.$description: 3XL text (30px). Use for hero or primary headings.

4xl.$description: 4XL text (36px). Use for display headings only.

xs.$description: Line height that `text-xs` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-xs/<leading>` overrides it.

sm.$description: Line height that `text-sm` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-sm/<leading>` overrides it.

base.$description: Line height that `text-base` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-base/<leading>` overrides it.

lg.$description: Line height that `text-lg` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-lg/<leading>` overrides it.

xl.$description: Line height that `text-xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-xl/<leading>` overrides it.

2xl.$description: Line height that `text-2xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-2xl/<leading>` overrides it.

3xl.$description: Line height that `text-3xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-3xl/<leading>` overrides it.

4xl.$description: Line height that `text-4xl` sets with its size. `leading-*` or `text-4xl/<leading>` overrides it.

tight.$description: Tight line height for headings. Not for paragraph text.

snug.$description: Snug line height. Not for long-form reading content.

normal.$description: Default line height for body text.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed line height for improved readability in long-form content.

loose.$description: Loose line height for highly spaced text. Not for dense UIs.

tight.$description: Tight letter spacing for large headings. Not for body text.

normal.$description: Default letter spacing. Use as baseline.

wide.$description: Wide letter spacing for small UI labels.

wider.$description: Wider letter spacing for all-caps or overline text.

widest.$description: Widest letter spacing, for the keyboard shortcuts of menus and the command palette.

medium.$description: Medium weight for UI labels and buttons.

bold.$description: Bold for headings and strong emphasis.

sans.$description: Secondary sans-serif typeface (Geist): Kbd keys and long-form editorial text. Loaded by next/font in lib/fonts.ts under --font-sans; this token describes that choice, it does not drive it (lint-font-tokens).

docs.do: Keep it for `Kbd` keys and long editorial content (`font-sans`).
docs.dont: Do not use it for the interface: all UI text is set in `font-mono`.

mono.$description: Typeface of the whole interface (JetBrains Mono), set on <html> with font-mono. Loaded by next/font in lib/fonts.ts under --font-mono; this token describes that choice, it does not drive it (lint-font-tokens).

docs.do: The default typeface of every UI component, set on `<html>`.
docs.dont: Do not change the typeface here alone: it is loaded by `next/font` in `lib/fonts.ts`, which `tokens:lint-fonts` checks against this token.

none.$description: Zero radius — square corners. Use for full-bleed or table elements.

xs.$description: Minimal rounding (0.4× base). Use for tags, badges, or tight UI chips.

sm.$description: Small rounding (0.6× base). Use for inputs, small buttons.

md.$description: Medium rounding (0.8× base). Use for default buttons and form controls.

lg.$description: Base rounding (1× = 0.625rem). Default for cards, panels, and shadcn --radius.

xl.$description: Larger rounding (1.4× base). Use for modals and prominent containers.

2xl.$description: Extra-large rounding (1.8× base). Use for floating panels.

3xl.$description: Very large rounding (2.2× base). Use sparingly for decorative containers.

4xl.$description: Maximum rounding (2.6× base). Use only for hero cards or large chips.

full.$description: Pill/full rounding. Use for pills, avatars, toggles.

docs.do: `radius.lg` for cards; `radius.md` for buttons; `radius.full` for avatars and pill badges.
docs.dont: No arbitrary values — always a token from the system.

xs.$description: Minimal lift for interactive elements. Not for decorative purposes.

sm.$description: Small lift for cards and hover states. Not for fixed navigation.

md.$description: Medium elevation for dropdowns and context menus. Not for inline content.

lg.$description: Large elevation for modals and side panels. Not for standard cards.

xl.$description: Extra-large elevation for full overlay panels. Not for inline components.

2xl.$description: Maximum elevation for toasts and high-priority overlays. Use sparingly.

inner.$description: Inner shadow for pressed, inset, or sunken element states. Not for raised elements.

docs.do: `shadow-sm` for cards, `shadow-md` for drop-downs, `shadow-lg` for modals.
docs.dont: Do not combine `shadow-inner` with an outer shadow on the same element.

instant.$description: No duration — for immediate state changes. Not for visual transitions.

fast.$description: Fast micro-interactions (100ms). Use for hover/focus feedback.

normal.$description: Standard transition duration (200ms). Default for most transitions.

slow.$description: Slow, deliberate transitions (300ms). Use for modals and drawers.

slower.$description: Slowest transitions (500ms). Use only for complex animations.

extra-slow.$description: Extra-slow duration (1000ms). Use for blink/pulse animations like caret blink.

default.$description: Standard ease-in-out. Default for all UI transitions.

in.$description: Ease-in curve. Use for elements exiting the screen.

out.$description: Ease-out curve. Use for elements entering the screen.

spring.$description: Spring overshoot. Use for playful or bouncy interactions only.

docs.do: `duration-normal` with `ease-default` as the universal starting point.
docs.dont: Never hard-code durations or easings — always use the CSS tokens.

disabled.$description: Opacity for disabled interactive elements. Not for placeholder or overlay use.

docs.do: Use `opacity-disabled` under the disabled-state variant: `disabled:opacity-disabled`, `data-disabled:opacity-disabled`, `aria-disabled:opacity-disabled`…
docs.dont: Do not write `disabled:opacity-50` (ESLint rejects it), and do not use it for secondary text — use `color.text.subtle`.

placeholder.$description: Deprecated: placeholder text was never faded. Form fields color it with color.text.subtle.

docs.do: Color the placeholder with `text-muted-foreground`, through the class its element answers to: `placeholder:text-muted-foreground` on an input or textarea, `data-placeholder:` on Select, `has-[option[value='']:checked]:` on NativeSelect.
docs.dont: Do not fade the placeholder with an opacity: default text at 0.5 is 3.70:1 on white, below 4.5:1.

placeholder.$deprecated: Form fields color their placeholder instead of fading it: use `placeholder:text-muted-foreground` (color.text.subtle). Faded default text drops to 3.70:1 on white.

overlay.$description: Deprecated: modal backdrops never read it. They use a 10% static-black scrim with a backdrop blur.

docs.do: Build a modal backdrop on `OVERLAY_BASE` (lib/overlay.ts): `bg-black/10` with `backdrop-blur-xs`, as Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet and Drawer do.
docs.dont: Do not darken the backdrop to `bg-black/80`: the page behind disappears, and the result drifts from the shadcn/ui v4 look agents reproduce.

overlay.$deprecated: Modal backdrops use shadcn/ui v4's scrim, `bg-black/10` with `backdrop-blur-xs` (OVERLAY_BASE in lib/overlay.ts); no opacity token drives it. At 0.8 the backdrop hid the page.

dropdown.$description: Dropdown menus. Renders above page content.

fixed.$description: Fixed position elements. Renders above sticky.

popover.$description: Popovers and tooltips of high priority. Renders above modals.

toast.$description: Toast notifications. Always visible above other layers.

tooltip.$description: Tooltips. Highest z-index to always appear on top.

docs.do: Always use the z-index tokens — never hard-coded numeric values.
docs.dont: Do not create new z-index levels outside this scale without approval.

sm.$description: Viewport width from which the `sm:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). Not a container width.

md.$description: Viewport width from which the `md:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). Not a container width.

lg.$description: Viewport width from which the `lg:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). Not a container width.

xl.$description: Viewport width from which the `xl:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). No component needs it yet; Tailwind compiles it regardless, so the token keeps its value on record for wide layouts.

2xl.$description: Viewport width from which the `2xl:` variant applies (mobile-first, min-width). No component needs it yet; Tailwind compiles it regardless, so the token keeps its value on record for wide layouts.

default.$description: Width of every plain border: `border`, `border-t`, `divide-x`… Not for focus rings, which use space.focus-ring-width.

chart-indicator.$description: Stroke of the dashed series indicator in chart tooltips. Not for component borders.

separation.$description: Ring painted in the background color around an element that overlaps another, cutting it out: stacked avatars, an avatar's badge. Not for borders or focus rings.

min.$description: Minimum pointer target (24px): WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), level AA. The clickable area of every control reaches it, or the control meets one of the exceptions listed in specs/foundations/size.md.

docs.do: Give a control drawn smaller than 24px a hit area of this size: `after:absolute after:inset-0 after:m-auto after:size-target` on a `relative` control, or `min-h-target min-w-target`.
docs.dont: Do not use it as a spacing value or to size an icon.
